Role of the DCM Between Tester, Basic Software, and Application

The DCM receives diagnostic requests from an external tester and responds to them. It implements the UDS services according to Table 7.5 [SWS_Dcm_00442] as well as OBD services such as $01 [SWS_Dcm_00243] and $09 [SWS_Dcm_00421]. Internally, three submodules work together:

  • The DSL submodule maintains the active session [SWS_Dcm_00022] and the active security level [SWS_Dcm_00020].
  • The DSD submodule analyzes the service identifier [SWS_Dcm_00192] and looks for the executing DSP function [SWS_Dcm_00221].
  • The DSP submodule executes the service and reports completion to the DSD [SWS_Dcm_00222].

The system boundary includes several neighboring modules and interfaces:

  • Mode Manager: The DCM manages the diagnostic modes [SWS_Dcm_00775]. For this purpose, it provides ModeDeclarationGroups, such as DcmDiagnosticSessionControl [SWS_Dcm_91019], DcmEcuReset [SWS_Dcm_00777], DcmControlDTCSetting [SWS_Dcm_00781], and DcmSecurityAccess [SWS_Dcm_01327]. For CommunicationControl, there is a dedicated group per network [SWS_Dcm_00780].
  • DEM: Diagnostic memory accesses run via the DEM, e.g., first Dem_SetDTCFilter, then Dem_GetNextFilteredDTC [SWS_Dcm_00835].
  • NvM: Persistent data such as DDDID definitions reside here [SWS_Dcm_00867].
  • ComM: It reports communication modes via callback [SWS_Dcm_00356].
  • CSM/KeyM: They answer crypto and certificate jobs asynchronously [SWS_Dcm_91076] [SWS_Dcm_91077].

Context diagram: The DCM mediates between PduR, ComM, DEM, NvM, CSM/KeyM, mode users, and application-side callouts. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00111], [SWS_Dcm_00775], [SWS_Dcm_91001], [SWS_Dcm_00614], SWS DCM p. 55

Initialization, Main Function, and Bootloader Transition

Dcm_Init [SWS_Dcm_00037] receives a pointer to Dcm_ConfigType with the post-build parameters (SWS DCM p. 275). The function initializes all global variables with configuration values [SWS_Dcm_00334]. Thereafter, the following initial state applies:

  • Security level is DCM_SEC_LEV_LOCKED [SWS_Dcm_00033].
  • The default session 0x01 is active [SWS_Dcm_00034].
  • All ROE events are set to "ROE cleared" [SWS_Dcm_00872].
  • ActiveDiagnostic is set to DCM_COMM_ACTIVE [SWS_Dcm_01069].
  • The attempt counters are read via Xxx_GetSecurityAttemptCounter [SWS_Dcm_01154].

During startup, the DCM also queries Dcm_GetProgConditions [SWS_Dcm_00536]. The return value DCM_WARM_START [SWS_Dcm_00987] indicates a return from the bootloader. In this case, a response ($50/$51) may still be due [SWS_Dcm_00537] (SWS DCM p. 299).

Ongoing work is performed by Dcm_MainFunction [SWS_Dcm_00053]. If an operation returns DCM_E_PENDING, the DCM calls it again, e.g., in the next cycle [SWS_Dcm_00760].

The transition to the bootloader proceeds as follows:

  1. The tester requests a session via 0x10 that triggers a bootloader jump [SWS_Dcm_00532] [SWS_Dcm_00592].
  2. Depending on the configuration, the DCM first sends NRC 0x78 [SWS_Dcm_00535].
  3. Interpretation: Thereafter, DcmEcuReset is likely to change to JUMPTOBOOTLOADER. Subsequently, the DCM calls Dcm_SetProgConditions [SWS_Dcm_00720] [SWS_Dcm_00543].
  4. In case of E_OK, another mode switch follows [SWS_Dcm_00719].

Dcm_ProgConditionsType transmits, among other things, ConnectionId, TesterAddress, Sid, and ResponseRequired [SWS_Dcm_00988].

Sequence diagram: Bootloader jump with saving of programming conditions and return with warm start detection. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00535], [SWS_Dcm_00720], [SWS_Dcm_00719], [SWS_Dcm_01184], [SWS_Dcm_00536], SWS DCM p. 283

The Path of a Request Through DSL, DSD, and DSP

Reception. The PduR starts reception with Dcm_StartOfReception [SWS_Dcm_00094]. With Dcm_CopyRxData, it copies the data into the DCM buffer [SWS_Dcm_00443]. It reports completion with Dcm_TpRxIndication [SWS_Dcm_00093]. The DSL forwards the request to the DSD only upon E_OK [SWS_Dcm_00111]. For generic connections, the DCM stores the source address from the MetaData [SWS_Dcm_00848].

Check in the DSD. The order of checks is based on ISO 14229-1 [SWS_Dcm_00827]:

  • An unknown service identifier leads to NRC 0x11 [SWS_Dcm_00197].
  • An unsupported subfunction leads to NRC 0x12 [SWS_Dcm_00273].
  • In addition, session [SWS_Dcm_00211], security level [SWS_Dcm_00217], and mode rules [SWS_Dcm_00773] are checked.
  • The application can intervene via Xxx_Indication [SWS_Dcm_00218] [SWS_Dcm_01341].
  • If the suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit is set, the positive response is omitted [SWS_Dcm_00200].

Activity diagram: Acceptance check in the DSD up to handover to the DSP (Interpretation: simplified sequence). Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00196], [SWS_Dcm_00677], [SWS_Dcm_00678], [SWS_Dcm_00815], [SWS_Dcm_00827]

Response and Confirmation.

  1. The DSD adds the response SID [SWS_Dcm_00223] and passes the response to the DSL [SWS_Dcm_00232]. The DSL forwards it to the PduR [SWS_Dcm_00237].
  2. The PduR retrieves the data using Dcm_CopyTxData [SWS_Dcm_00092].
  3. After Dcm_TpTxConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_00351], the confirmation reaches the DSP via DspInternal_DcmConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_00236]. The application receives it via Xxx_Confirmation [SWS_Dcm_00741].

The DCM can send large responses page by page via the paged buffer [SWS_Dcm_00028]. If the next page is not yet ready, Dcm_CopyTxData returns the value BUFREQ_E_BUSY [SWS_Dcm_01186] (SWS DCM p. 481).

Sequence diagram: Reception, check, execution, and confirmed positive response. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00111], [SWS_Dcm_00235], [SWS_Dcm_00236], SWS DCM p. 479

Asynchronous Callouts, OpStatus, and Response Pending

Asynchronous application interfaces receive an Dcm_OpStatusType [SWS_Dcm_00984]:

  • On the first call, the value is DCM_INITIAL [SWS_Dcm_00527].
  • After a DCM_E_PENDING, DCM_PENDING follows [SWS_Dcm_00530].
  • A cancellation occurs with DCM_CANCEL [SWS_Dcm_00735]. The DCM ignores the return value of this call [SWS_Dcm_01413].

The configuration defines whether an interface operates synchronously or asynchronously. An example is Xxx_ReadData: there is a synchronous variant [SWS_Dcm_00793] and an asynchronous one [SWS_Dcm_91006]. Memory accesses use dedicated return types such as Dcm_ReturnReadMemoryType [SWS_Dcm_00985] (SWS DCM p. 281).

Response Pending. The DSL monitors the time limits P2ServerMax and P2*ServerMax [SWS_Dcm_00027]. If processing takes longer, it sends NRC 0x78 [SWS_Dcm_00024] (SWS DCM p. 433). The application can also force NRC 0x78 immediately by returning DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP [SWS_Dcm_00528]. After the transmission confirmation, the DCM then calls the operation with DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK [SWS_Dcm_00529]. The number of consecutive NRC 0x78 allowed is limited [SWS_Dcm_00120] [SWS_Dcm_01567].

Sequence diagram: OpStatus protocol of an asynchronous routine with pending, forced RCR-RP, and final result. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00527], [SWS_Dcm_00529], [SWS_Dcm_00401], [SWS_Dcm_00668], [SWS_Dcm_00669], SWS DCM p. 281

Session, Security Level, and Authentication as Access Control

Sessions. The DCM implements UDS 0x10 [SWS_Dcm_00250]. An unconfigured session type leads to NRC 0x12 [SWS_Dcm_00307]. The new session takes effect only upon transmission confirmation. At the same time, the DCM sets the new P2 values and performs the mode switch [SWS_Dcm_00311] (SWS DCM p. 107). The DCM returns to the default session in two ways:

  • on an S3Server timeout [SWS_Dcm_00140] (SWS DCM p. 492),
  • when the application calls Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession [SWS_Dcm_01062].

A session change has side effects:

  • Active IO controls are terminated [SWS_Dcm_00858].
  • In the default session, periodic DIDs stop [SWS_Dcm_01107].
  • Started ROE events transition to "ROE stopped" [SWS_Dcm_00879].

State diagram: Lifecycle of the diagnostic session from start to return to the default session. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00034], [SWS_Dcm_00311], [SWS_Dcm_00140], [SWS_Dcm_00520], [SWS_Dcm_00532], [SWS_Dcm_00978]

SecurityAccess (0x27) [SWS_Dcm_00252]:

  • For requestSeed, the DCM calls Xxx_GetSeed [SWS_Dcm_00323].
  • For sendKey, it calls Xxx_CompareKey [SWS_Dcm_00324]. In case of E_OK, it sets the new level [SWS_Dcm_00325] and reports it via DcmSecurityAccess [SWS_Dcm_01329].
  • Failed attempts lead to a delay time starting from a threshold [SWS_Dcm_00660] [SWS_Dcm_01350]. A successful sendKey or an expired delay timer resets the counter [SWS_Dcm_01357].
  • Each level change terminates active IO controls [SWS_Dcm_00859].

Authentication (0x29). The DCM implements the Authentication service [SWS_Dcm_01559]. It maintains a separate authentication state per connection [SWS_Dcm_01477]. After successful certificate verification [SWS_Dcm_01468] and proof of ownership [SWS_Dcm_01511], the connection transitions to the "authenticated" state [SWS_Dcm_01528]. Upon idle or S3Server timeout, it falls back to the "deauthenticated" state [SWS_Dcm_01482] [SWS_Dcm_01483]. The configured deauthentication role then applies [SWS_Dcm_01485] (SWS DCM p. 69).

Communication Modes, Protocols, and Event-Driven Responses

Communication Modes. The ComM controls via callback what the DCM is allowed to send:

  • Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered disables reception and transmission [SWS_Dcm_00148].
  • Dcm_ComM_SilentComModeEntered disables transmission [SWS_Dcm_00153].
  • Dcm_ComM_FullComModeEntered enables everything [SWS_Dcm_00157].

Periodic transmissions and ROE are permitted only in Full Communication [SWS_Dcm_00123] [SWS_Dcm_00133]. The DCM discards events outside this mode [SWS_Dcm_00125] [SWS_Dcm_00135]. Conversely, the DCM reports active diagnostics to the ComM [SWS_Dcm_01373]. The application can disable this notification via Dcm_SetActiveDiagnostic [SWS_Dcm_01068].

State diagram: Permissions of the DCM per ComM communication mode. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00148], [SWS_Dcm_00149], [SWS_Dcm_00154], [SWS_Dcm_00159], SWS DCM p. 499

Protocols. With the first request of a protocol, the DCM calls Xxx_StartProtocol [SWS_Dcm_00036]. If the call does not return E_OK, the DCM responds with NRC 0x22 [SWS_Dcm_00674]. A protocol of higher priority may preempt an ongoing one [SWS_Dcm_00015] [SWS_Dcm_00459]. The application is informed of this via Xxx_StopProtocol (SWS DCM p. 495). The DCM processes OBD requests in parallel with an ongoing UDS request [SWS_Dcm_01367].

ResponseOnEvent. Each RoeEvent knows the states "cleared", "stopped", and "started" [SWS_Dcm_00871]. Events are triggered via Dcm_TriggerOnEvent [SWS_Dcm_00920] or via status changes of DTCs [SWS_Dcm_00914]. The ServiceToRespondTo then due runs like a normal request [SWS_Dcm_00922].

Behavior in the event of an error

During Reception.

  • If a request exceeds the buffer, Dcm_StartOfReception returns the value BUFREQ_E_OVFL [SWS_Dcm_00444].
  • With TpSduLength 0, the function returns BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK [SWS_Dcm_00642] (SWS DCM p. 57).
  • If Dcm_TpRxIndication reports an error, the DCM does not evaluate the data [SWS_Dcm_00344].
  • It can reject further requests during ongoing processing [SWS_Dcm_00557]. Depending on the configuration, it responds to them with NRC 0x21 [SWS_Dcm_00789].

During Transmission. Dcm_TpTxConfirmation releases the transmit buffer [SWS_Dcm_00352] and terminates the ongoing error handling [SWS_Dcm_00353] (ErrorDescription p. 26). For failed transmissions, [SWS_Dcm_00118] applies. If a request is preempted, the DCM aborts transmissions at the PduR [SWS_Dcm_00079] [SWS_Dcm_00575]. It terminates ongoing NvM jobs with NvM_CancelJobs [SWS_Dcm_01048].

Errors from Application and Neighboring Modules.

  • If a callout returns E_NOT_OK or DCM_READ_FAILED, the DCM sends the ErrorCode as an NRC, e.g., [SWS_Dcm_00668] [SWS_Dcm_00644].
  • The value range and unexpected returns are governed by [SWS_Dcm_01414] and [SWS_Dcm_01415] (SWS DCM p. 346).
  • If Dem_ClearDTC reports DEM_CLEAR_FAILED, NRC 0x22 follows [SWS_Dcm_00704]. In case of DEM_WRONG_DTC, NRC 0x31 follows [SWS_Dcm_00708].
  • If Dcm_SetProgConditions returns the value E_NOT_OK, the DCM does not request a reset [SWS_Dcm_01181]. Upon a bootloader jump, it additionally reports a DET error [SWS_Dcm_01185].
  • The error types are specified in [SWS_Dcm_00044] and [SWS_Dcm_01416].

Further detailed evidence

  • [SWS_Dcm_00111], SWS DCM p. 55: Transition from TP reception to service processing.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00827]: Mandatory checking order according to ISO 14229-1.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00528], [SWS_Dcm_00530]: OpStatus protocol for all asynchronous callouts.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00311], SWS DCM p. 272: Session change and reset by the application.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00775], SWS DCM p. 483: Role of the DCM as mode manager.
  • [SWS_Dcm_01477], [SWS_Dcm_01522]: Authentication state per connection and role check.
  • Release difference 1: For R20-11, the signature is Dcm_CsmAsyncJobFinished(Csm_ResultType result) [SWS_Dcm_91076]. The more recent documentation section shows jobId and Crypto_ResultType (SWS DCM p. 279). The requirement is authoritative.
  • Release difference 2: In R20-11, the upload callout is named Xxx_ProcessRequestUpload [SWS_Dcm_00756]. The later documentation section names it Dcm_ProcessRequestUpload (SWS DCM p. 308).

AI-generated guide based on the specification excerpts for the DCM (classic, R20-11). The linked requirements are normative; documentation sections may originate from later releases. Identified interpretations must be verified before use.

Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM)

The DCM implements unified diagnostic services according to ISO 14229-1 (UDS) and ISO 15765-4 (OBD). It manages diagnostic sessions, security levels, and service routing.

function Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus [SWS_Dcm_00614] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus (uint32 DTC, Dem_UdsStatusByteType DTCStatusOld, Dem_UdsStatusByteType DTCStatusNew);

Triggers on changes of the UDS status byte. Allows to trigger on ROE Event for subservice On DTCStatusChanged.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 5b03acaadde8 Provenance

The function Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus ([SWS_Dcm_00614]) is available via the header Dcm_Dem.h and serves to notify about changes to the UDS status byte. It enables the DCM to trigger a Response-on-Event event (ROE event) for the subservice On DTCStatusChanged ([SWS_Dcm_00614]).

Usage and Concurrency

The interface has the service ID 0x2B, operates synchronously, and is specified as reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_00614]). Upon the call, the following parameters are passed:

  • DTC (input parameter, uint32): The DTC with which the status change is associated ([SWS_Dcm_00614]).
  • DTCStatusOld (input parameter, Dem_UdsStatusByteType): The UDS status byte before the change ([SWS_Dcm_00614]).
  • DTCStatusNew (input parameter, Dem_UdsStatusByteType): The UDS status byte after the change ([SWS_Dcm_00614]).

Inout or out parameters do not exist ([SWS_Dcm_00614]). As a return value of type Std_ReturnType, the function returns E_OK without exception ([SWS_Dcm_00614]); specific error codes or alternative status values are not provided.

Interaction and Constraints

In interaction with the diagnostic memory, a mandatory exception applies: if the DCM is currently processing a request to clear the event memory (Clear EventMemory), it must ignore the callback Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus ([SWS_Dcm_01410]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification requirements of AUTOSAR release R20-11.

function Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish [SWS_Dcm_91088] 📄 PDF

void Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish (BndM_BlockIdType BlockId, BndM_ResultType result);

Called by BndM to indicate that a block write operation has finished.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 54f0df9d836a Provenance

The function Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish ([SWS_Dcm_91088]) serves as a feedback interface and is called by module BndM to indicate that a block write operation has ended. The call is performed synchronously (service ID 0x7a), returns no return value, and is available via the header file Dcm.h.

Parameters and Semantics

  • BlockId (BndM_BlockIdType): Passes the identification of the block whose write process was completed.
  • result (BndM_ResultType): Transmits the result of the performed block write operation to the DCM.

Interaction and Error Handling

If an atomic write operation was previously triggered in the BndM by the DCM, the passed result directly controls the diagnostic response of the DCM:

  • If Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish is called with parameter value result = E_OK, the DCM sends a positive diagnostic response ([SWS_Dcm_01584]).
  • If the function is called with result = E_NOT_OK, the DCM sends a negative diagnostic response (NRC) 0x72 (generalProgrammingFailure) ([SWS_Dcm_01585]).

Concurrency and Limitations

The interface is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Dcm_91088]). The caller must ensure that concurrent or interrupting calls to this function do not occur.

function Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole [SWS_Dcm_91069] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole (uint16 connectionId, Dcm_AuthenticationRoleType deauthenticatedRole);

Sets a new role used in deauthenticated state for that connection. The set role is valid until the connection switches into authenticated state or the ECU is reset.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 7b81c1932854 Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous and reentrant service function Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole ([SWS_Dcm_91069]) assigns a new role for the deauthenticated state (deauthenticated state) to a diagnostic connection. The interface is provided via header Dcm.h.

  • connectionId: Unique identifier of the diagnostic connection for which the role is to be set.
  • deauthenticatedRole: Role of type Dcm_AuthenticationRoleType to be assigned.
  • Return value: Always returns E_OK ([SWS_Dcm_91069]). Specific error values, DET or DEM notifications are not defined in the specification.

State Conditions and Lifetime

Defined conditions apply to the invocation and validity of the role:

  • Call condition: The DCM processes the call of Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole exclusively if the connection in question is already in state deauthenticated state ([SWS_Dcm_01487]).
  • Role adoption: If the connection is in this state, the DCM adopts the passed role as the new role for the deauthenticated state of this connection ([SWS_Dcm_01486]).
  • Validity period: The configured role remains valid until the connection transitions to the authenticated state or an ECU reset occurs ([SWS_Dcm_91069]).
  • Reset: If the connection performs a state transition to authenticated state, the role set by the SWC is discarded ([SWS_Dcm_01488]).

function Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession [SWS_Dcm_00520] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession (void);

The call to this function allows the application to reset the current session to Default session. Example: Automatic termination of an extended diagnostic session upon exceeding of a speed limit.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 307e21701c54 Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The function Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession ([SWS_Dcm_00520]) enables the application to reset the currently active diagnostic session synchronously to the default session (Default Session). A typical use case is the automated termination of an extended diagnostic session when a vehicle-specific speed threshold is exceeded.

The function expects no pass parameters and declares Std_ReturnType as its return value, whereby according to the specification E_OK is always returned.

Concurrency and Error Handling

The call is specified as reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_00520]) and is accessible via the header file Dcm.h. Specific error codes, fallback values, or separate DET/DEM error notifications are not defined for this interface.

Interaction and System Integration

Calling Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession not only resets the internal session, but additionally triggers the mode switch of ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype DcmDiagnosticSessionControl ([SWS_Dcm_01062]). In this process, the system call SchM_Switch_<bsnp>_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl(RTE_MODE_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl_DCM_DEFAULT_SESSION) is made, notifying dependent BSW modules and software components synchronously about the switch to the Default Session.

function Dcm_TriggerOnEvent [SWS_Dcm_00521] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_TriggerOnEvent (uint8 RoeEventId);

The call to this function allows to trigger an event linked to a ResponseOnEvent request. On the function call, the DCM will execute the associated service if the corresponding Mode of the Roe EventId is 'ROE started'.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: cb6386dedeb1 Provenance

The API function Dcm_TriggerOnEvent ([SWS_Dcm_00521]) serves to trigger an event that is linked to a ResponseOnEvent (ROE) request. The function is declared via the header file Dcm.h.

Usage and Semantics

  • Call context and concurrency: The function operates synchronously and is designed to be reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_00521]).
  • Passed parameters: RoeEventId (of type uint8) is passed, which represents the unique identifier of the event to be triggered ([SWS_Dcm_00521]).
  • Return values: The function returns Std_ReturnType. With a valid identifier RoeEventId, E_OK is returned; if the value of RoeEventId is invalid, the function returns E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00521]).

Interaction and Conditions

When Dcm_TriggerOnEvent is called, the DCM executes the assigned diagnostic service only if the corresponding mode of the RoeEventId is in the "ROE started" state ([SWS_Dcm_00521]). Accordingly, upon call of the function, the DCM triggers an event for this RoeEvent provided that the passed event is active ([SWS_Dcm_00920]).

Error handling

If an invalid event identifier is passed to RoeEventId, the function reports the error directly via the return value E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00521]). Additional error notifications via DET or DEM are not specified for this call.

function Dcm_StartOfReception [SWS_Dcm_00094] 📄 PDF

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_StartOfReception (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType TpSduLength, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);

This function is called at the start of receiving an N-SDU. The N-SDU might be fragmented into multiple N-PDUs (FF with one or more following CFs) or might consist of a single N-PDU (SF). The service shall provide the currently available maximum buffer size when invoked with TpSdu Length equal to 0. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: bb416eae6ee7 Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_StartOfReception [SWS_Dcm_00094] is called at the start of reception of an N-SDU – both for single messages (Single Frame, SF) and for fragmented messages (First Frame, FF followed by Consecutive Frames, CF). It can be executed in interrupt context [SWS_Dcm_00094].

Parameters and Return Values

  • id identifies the received I-PDU [SWS_Dcm_00094].
  • info references payload and MetaData of the first or single frame, or is NULL_PTR [SWS_Dcm_00094]. For generic connections, the metadata conveys, among other things, SOURCE_ADDRESS_16 [SWS_Dcm_00094], [SWS_Dcm_00848], and optionally TARGET_ADDRESS_16 for address verification [SWS_Dcm_01347].
  • TpSduLength passes the total length of the N-SDU to be received. If TpSduLength == 0 is passed, the API returns BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK and takes no further action [SWS_Dcm_00642].
  • Upon acceptance (BUFREQ_OK), bufferSizePtr returns the available reception buffer, which is used by the transport protocol to calculate the Block Size (BS) [SWS_Dcm_00094]. Upon rejection, the value remains unchanged [SWS_Dcm_00094].
  • Return values: BUFREQ_OK accepts the connection; BUFREQ_E_OVFL aborts reception if the requested length is greater than the buffer available in the DCM [SWS_Dcm_00094], [SWS_Dcm_00443], [SWS_Dcm_00444]; BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK rejects the connection [SWS_Dcm_00094].

Interaction and Concurrency

If an ongoing diagnostic request is being processed, the DCM rejects new requests via the same connection (DcmDslConnection) with BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK, but accepts concurrent TesterPresent requests with BUFREQ_OK [SWS_Dcm_00557]. For requests via a different connection, the configuration parameter DcmDslDiagRespOnSecondDeclinedRequest controls whether acceptance is made with BUFREQ_OK [SWS_Dcm_00788] or rejection with BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK [SWS_Dcm_00790]. The call also stops the session timer S3Server for the duration of the reception [SWS_Dcm_00141]. After successful acceptance, Dcm_CopyRxData copies the data stepwise into the DCM buffer [SWS_Dcm_00443].

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

function Dcm_CopyRxData [SWS_Dcm_00556] 📄 PDF

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_CopyRxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);

This function is called to provide the received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer. Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data. The size of the remaining buffer is written to the position indicated by bufferSizePtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: ebeb3699129d Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous function Dcm_CopyRxData ([SWS_Dcm_00556]) is called by the lower transport layer to transfer received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) stepwise to the DCM. Each call provides the respective next part of the I-PDU data.

  • id: Identifies the received I-PDU ([SWS_Dcm_00556]).
  • info: Points to a structure with the source buffer (SduDataPtr) and the number of bytes to be copied (SduLength) ([SWS_Dcm_00556]).
  • bufferSizePtr: Holds the remaining free buffer size in the DCM receive buffer after the copying process ([SWS_Dcm_00556], [SWS_Dcm_00443]).

Interaction and Buffer Query

A prerequisite for the copying process is a successful receive start: if Dcm_StartOfReception returned the value BUFREQ_OK, subsequent calls of Dcm_CopyRxData copy the data from parameter info into the internal DCM buffer and update bufferSizePtr with the remaining space ([SWS_Dcm_00443]).

In addition, the function supports a pure buffer query: if Dcm_CopyRxData is called with a SduLength value of 0, SduDataPtr may be a NULL_PTR ([SWS_Dcm_00556]). In this case, the call returns BUFREQ_OK and outputs the available remaining size of the receive buffer via bufferSizePtr ([SWS_Dcm_00996]).

Error Handling and Concurrency

  • Return values: BUFREQ_OK signals successful copying or the successful buffer query; BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK indicates that the data could not be copied due to an error that occurred ([SWS_Dcm_00556]).
  • Execution context: The function is designed to be reentrant and may be called in the interrupt context ([SWS_Dcm_00556]).

This usage note is based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

function Dcm_TpRxIndication [SWS_Dcm_00093] 📄 PDF

void Dcm_TpRxIndication (PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);

Called after an I-PDU has been received via the TP API, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 259f07cb3f94 Provenance

use

The synchronous service function Dcm_TpRxIndication ([SWS_Dcm_00093]) is called after reception of an I-PDU via the TP API, typically by the module PduR ([SWS_Dcm_00112]). It reports to the DCM whether the transmission was completed successfully. The function has no return value and has the following input parameters:

  • id (PduIdType): Identification of the received I-PDU ([SWS_Dcm_00093]).
  • result (Std_ReturnType): Result of the reception process ([SWS_Dcm_00093]).

Error handling

If Dcm_TpRxIndication is called with a value for result other than E_OK, the DCM module must not evaluate the buffer assigned to the passed I-PDU ([SWS_Dcm_00344]). Specific DET or DEM error notifications are not listed in the function definition.

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is designed to be reentrant and may explicitly be called in interrupt context ([SWS_Dcm_00093]).

Interaction

Calling Dcm_TpRxIndication controls internal forwarding and state handling in the DCM:

  • The DSL submodule forwards received diagnostic data to the DSD submodule only after a call to Dcm_TpRxIndication with the parameter value Result = E_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00111]).
  • If Dcm_TpRxIndication is called with Result = E_OK for a TesterPresent command with suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit set (SID 0x3E, subfunction 0x80), the DSL submodule resets the session timeout timer S3Server ([SWS_Dcm_00112]).
  • For the same suppressed TesterPresent command (SID 0x3E, subfunction 0x80), the DSL submodule does not forward the request to the DSD submodule for further interpretation ([SWS_Dcm_00113]).

This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR Classic specification release R20-11 and was created automatically.

function Dcm_CopyTxData [SWS_Dcm_00092] 📄 PDF

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_CopyTxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, const RetryInfoType* retry, PduLengthType* availableDataPtr);

This function is called to acquire the transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data unless retry->TpDataState is TP_ DATARETRY. In this case the function restarts to copy the data beginning at the offset from the current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to the position indicated by availableDataPtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 9b6b85e1a0ce Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_CopyTxData ([SWS_Dcm_00092]) is called by an underlying transport protocol module (TP) to retrieve transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). The call may also take place in the interrupt context ([SWS_Dcm_00092]).

Usage and Parameters

  • id: Identifies the I-PDU to be transmitted ([SWS_Dcm_00092]).
  • info: Provides the destination buffer (SduDataPtr) and the number of bytes to be copied (SduLength). If SduLength is 0, the call serves to signal status changes via retry or to query available data; in this case, SduDataPtr may be a NULL_PTR ([SWS_Dcm_00092]).
  • retry: Serves to confirm or retry the transmission. If retry is equal to NULL_PTR, data may be removed from the buffer immediately after copying. Otherwise, TpDataState controls the behavior: TP_CONFPENDING retains data in the buffer for error recovery, TP_DATACONF confirms previously copied data for release, and TP_DATARETRY re-copies data starting from the offset specified by TxTpDataCnt ([SWS_Dcm_00092]).
  • availableDataPtr: Reports the remaining number of available bytes in the transmit buffer (e.g., for TP modules with dynamic length support) ([SWS_Dcm_00092]). Under no circumstances may this value exceed the number of bytes still to be sent ([SWS_Dcm_00350]).

Return Values and Error Handling

  • BUFREQ_OK: Data was copied completely into the buffer as requested ([SWS_Dcm_00092], [SWS_Dcm_00346]).
  • BUFREQ_E_BUSY: The requested amount of transmit data is not available; no data was copied. The lower layer can repeat the call later ([SWS_Dcm_00092]).
  • BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK: The request failed; no data was copied ([SWS_Dcm_00092]).

Interaction and Constraints

If Dcm_CopyTxData returns the status BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK, the transmit request previously initiated by PduR_DcmTransmit() has not yet completed. Only a final error notification via Dcm_TpTxConfirmation() by the transport protocol terminates the service and allows starting a new transmission via PduR_DcmTransmit() ([SWS_Dcm_00350]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

function Dcm_TpTxConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_00351] 📄 PDF

void Dcm_TpTxConfirmation (PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);

This function is called after the I-PDU has been transmitted on its network, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d3f211e63fa5 Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant callback function Dcm_TpTxConfirmation ([SWS_Dcm_00351]) is called as soon as an I-PDU has been transmitted on the network. The transmitted I-PDU is identified via the input parameter id, while result reports the success or failure of the transmission. The function has no return value and may also be called in interrupt context ([SWS_Dcm_00351]).

Error Handling and Transmission Abort

In the event of a failed transmission or a negative confirmation via result, the DSD submodule does not retry the transmission of the diagnostic response ([SWS_Dcm_00118]). If data transfer was previously aborted via Dcm_CopyTxData with BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK, the ongoing transmit request is only completed when the transport protocol confirms the abort by calling Dcm_TpTxConfirmation with an error status; only then can a new transmission be initiated via PduR_DcmTransmit() ([SWS_Dcm_00350]).

Interaction and State Management

Calling Dcm_TpTxConfirmation triggers significant follow-up actions and state cleanups in the DCM:

  • The DCM module unlocks the associated transmit buffer ([SWS_Dcm_00352]).
  • The timeout monitorings for page buffers as well as P2ServerMax and P2*ServerMax are stopped ([SWS_Dcm_00353]).
  • The DcmPduId, which has been locked since reception, is released again so that subsequent requests can be received on the same connection ([SWS_Dcm_00241]).
  • If a positive or negative response other than NRC 0x78 was confirmed, the diagnostic request is considered formally completed ([SWS_Dcm_01378]).
  • The running protocol is not stopped upon confirmation of the response initiated by the DSL submodule ([SWS_Dcm_00624]).
  • If the confirmation for a positive EcuReset response is received, the DCM ignores all further requests during further reset processing ([SWS_Dcm_00834]).

This usage note was created automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

The callback function Dcm_TxConfirmation ([SWS_Dcm_01092]) is called by an underlying communication interface module to confirm the transmission of a PDU or the failure of the transmission process to the DCM. The function operates synchronously, has no return value (void), and is defined via Dcm.h with the service ID 0x40.

The input parameters include:

  • TxPduId: Identifier of the transmitted PDU.
  • result: Result of the transmission process (E_OK on successful transmission of the PDU, E_NOT_OK on failed transmission).

According to [SWS_Dcm_01092], the function is reentrant for different PDU IDs, but non-reentrant for the same TxPduId. In addition, the call may take place in interrupt context.

Interaction and Error Handling

An error during transmission is indicated directly via the parameter result with the return value E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Dcm_01092]). In the case of periodic transmissions (PeriodicTransmission), the DCM is likewise called via Dcm_TxConfirmation to indicate the transmission result ([SWS_Dcm_01073]).

function Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered [SWS_Dcm_00356] 📄 PDF

void Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered (uint8 NetworkId);

This call informs the Dcm module about a ComM mode change to COMM_NO_ COMMUNICATION.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d9b540db611a Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered ([SWS_Dcm_00356]) informs the DCM module about a mode switch of ComM to the state COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION. The network affected by the mode switch is identified via the input parameter NetworkId ([SWS_Dcm_00356]). The interface has no return value and is provided via the header file Dcm_ComM.h ([SWS_Dcm_00356]).

Impact on Communication

As a result of the call, the DCM switches off all communication transmissions for the affected network, completely disabling both reception and transmission of messages ([SWS_Dcm_00148]). In detail, this includes:

  • the deactivation of normal transmissions ([SWS_Dcm_00151]),
  • the deactivation of response-on-event transmissions ([SWS_Dcm_00149]), as well as
  • the deactivation of periodic transmissions within the scope of service ReadDataByPeriodicIdentifier ([SWS_Dcm_00150]).

Consequently, the DCM module must no longer call the function PduR_DcmTransmit() after execution of the call ([SWS_Dcm_00152]).

Error Handling and Special Cases

If the function is called with a NetworkId that does not correspond to any ComM channel referenced in the DCM (defined via configuration parameter DcmDslProtocolComMChannelRef), the DCM aborts processing and returns without further action ([SWS_Dcm_01324]).

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_ComM_SilentComModeEntered ([SWS_Dcm_00358], service ID 0x22) informs the DCM module about a mode switch of the Communication Manager (ComM) into the communication mode COMM_SILENT_COMMUNICATION. The declaration is available via the header file Dcm_ComM.h.

Usage and Parameters

The call takes place with the input parameter NetworkId (data type uint8), which identifies the network affected by the mode switch ([SWS_Dcm_00358]). A return value is not present (return type void).

Interaction and Transmission Behavior

Upon entering this mode, the DCM disables all transmission activities so that message dispatch is completely prevented ([SWS_Dcm_00153]). This includes the following transmission types:

  • Disabling of all ResponseOnEvent transmissions ([SWS_Dcm_00154]).
  • Disabling of periodic message transmissions (ReadDataByPeriodicIdentifier or periodicId) ([SWS_Dcm_00155]).
  • Disabling of normal diagnostic message transmissions ([SWS_Dcm_00156]).

Error Handling and Boundary Conditions

If Dcm_ComM_SilentComModeEntered is called with a NetworkId that does not belong to any ComM channel configured in the DCM (via the configuration parameter DcmDslProtocolComMChannelRef), the DCM performs no actions and returns immediately ([SWS_Dcm_01325]).

The affected network is passed via the input parameter NetworkId; the function has neither input/output nor return parameters [SWS_Dcm_00360].

Interaction and Communication Enablement

The call enables all communication for the affected channel so that both the reception and transmission of messages are active [SWS_Dcm_00157]. This includes the following transmission types:

  • normal transmissions of diagnostic responses [SWS_Dcm_00161],
  • ResponseOnEvent transmissions [SWS_Dcm_00159], as well as
  • periodic transmissions via ReadDataByPeriodicIdentifier [SWS_Dcm_00160].

After execution of this function, the DCM executes internal handling routines such as DslInternal_ResponseOnOneDataByPeriodicId() and DslInternal_ResponseOnOneEvent() without restrictions [SWS_Dcm_00162].

Sequence Conditions and Error Behavior

The DCM must wait for the mode indication Dcm_ComM_FullComModeEntered from the ComM before initiating the transmission of a diagnostic response. The maximum waiting time from the time of request reception must not exceed P2ServerMax [SWS_Dcm_01142].

If the function is called with a NetworkId that is not assigned to any ComM channel referenced in the DCM via the configuration parameter DcmDslProtocolComMChannelRef, the DCM returns immediately without performing further actions [SWS_Dcm_01326].

function Dcm_ReadMemory [SWS_Dcm_00539] 📄 PDF

Dcm_ReturnReadMemoryType Dcm_ReadMemory (Dcm_OpStatusType OpStatus, uint8 MemoryIdentifier, uint32 MemoryAddress, uint32 MemorySize, uint8* MemoryData, Dcm_NegativeResponseCodeType* ErrorCode);

The Dcm_ReadMemory callout is used to request memory data identified by the parameter memoryAddress and memorySize from the UDS request message. This service is needed for the implementation of UDS services: • ReadMemoryByAddress • RequestUpload • ReadDataByIdentifier (in case of Dynamical DID defined by memory address) • TransferData

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 7222f5d1c980 Provenance

The callout function Dcm_ReadMemory ([SWS_Dcm_00539], declared in Dcm_Externals.h) is called by the DCM module to retrieve memory data based on starting address (MemoryAddress) and length (MemorySize) from a UDS request. The parameter MemoryIdentifier serves to distinguish memory areas and must be set to 0 if not used. The read result is written to the DCM diagnostic buffer (MemoryData).

Scope of Application and Interaction

The function is required to implement multiple UDS services ([SWS_Dcm_00539]):

  • ReadMemoryByAddress (0x23): After successful verification of the request data, the DCM calls the callout ([SWS_Dcm_00495]).
  • ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22): For DIDs dynamically defined via memory addresses in the range 0xF200 to 0xF3FF, the DCM reads the data via this callout ([SWS_Dcm_00653]).
  • RequestUpload and TransferData: Provision of the requested memory data for upload and transfer operations ([SWS_Dcm_00539]).

Asynchronous Semantics and Flow Control

The function is executed asynchronously and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Dcm_00539]). The call status is controlled via OpStatus (DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, DCM_CANCEL, or DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK). Possible return values of type Dcm_ReturnReadMemoryType ([SWS_Dcm_00985]) are:

  • DCM_READ_OK: The read operation was completed successfully.
  • DCM_READ_PENDING: The operation is still ongoing; another call is required for completion.
  • DCM_READ_FORCE_RCRRP: The operation is still ongoing; the DCM immediately initiates the transmission of a Response Pending message (NRC 0x78) and suspends further calls until the transmission completes ([SWS_Dcm_00839]). After transmission confirmation, the DCM calls the function from Dcm_MainFunction again with OpStatus = DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00840]).
  • DCM_READ_FAILED: The read operation has failed.

Error handling

If the callout returns DCM_READ_FAILED, the negative return code must be provided via the output parameter ErrorCode. The DCM module then sends a negative response with this NRC ([SWS_Dcm_00539], [SWS_Dcm_00644]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.

Call Context and Semantics

The function is asynchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). It is declared via the header file Dcm_Externals.h ([SWS_Dcm_00540]). Upon reception and successful verification of a request for WriteMemoryByAddress, the DCM calls this callout ([SWS_Dcm_00491]).

Parameters and Return Values

  • OpStatus: Controls execution with the values DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, DCM_CANCEL, or DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00540]).
  • MemoryIdentifier and MemoryAddress: Specify the block or destination address; if not used (e.g., in case of compressed data), they must be set to 0 ([SWS_Dcm_00540]).
  • MemoryData: Points to the user data to be written in the DCM diagnostic buffer ([SWS_Dcm_00540]).

A value of type Dcm_ReturnWriteMemoryType ([SWS_Dcm_00986]) is returned as status:

  • DCM_WRITE_OK: Write operation was successful ([SWS_Dcm_00540]).
  • DCM_WRITE_PENDING: Write operation is not yet completed; a subsequent call is expected ([SWS_Dcm_00540]).
  • DCM_WRITE_FORCE_RCRRP: Triggers the immediate transmission of a Response Pending (NRC 0x78). The DCM pauses further calls until transmission confirmation ([SWS_Dcm_00837]) and subsequently calls the function again from Dcm_MainFunction with OpStatus = DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00838]).

Error handling

If the function returns DCM_WRITE_FAILED, the DCM module sends a negative response with the NRC value set in output parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_00540], [SWS_Dcm_00643]).

Std_ReturnType Dcm_SetProgConditions (Dcm_OpStatusType OpStatus, const Dcm_ProgConditionsType* ProgConditions);

The Dcm_SetProgConditions callout allows the integrator to store relevant information prior to jumping to bootloader / jump due to ECUReset request. The context parameter are defined in Dcm_ProgConditionsType.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 9d7b25f13111 Provenance

Usage and Call Context

The callout Dcm_SetProgConditions ([SWS_Dcm_00543]) allows the integrator to save relevant state information prior to a jump into the bootloader or prior to a reset. The DCM provides the parameters in the structure Dcm_ProgConditionsType ([SWS_Dcm_00988]). If a UDS service 0x10 with subfunction 0x02 is received, the DCM sets, among others, the flags ReprogramingRequest as well as, if required, ResponseRequired before the call ([SWS_Dcm_01182]). If DcmSendRespPendOnRestart is configured to TRUE and a boot session is active, the call occurs after successful transmission of NRC 0x78 ([SWS_Dcm_00535]).

Asynchronous Semantics and Return Values

The function is non-reentrant and behaves asynchronously ([SWS_Dcm_00543]). The call is performed specifying the operation status OpStatus (DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, DCM_CANCEL, or DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK):

  • E_OK: The programming conditions were successfully saved. The DCM then triggers the mode switch of the prototype DcmEcuReset to EXECUTE ([SWS_Dcm_00719], [SWS_Dcm_01163], [SWS_Dcm_01180]).
  • DCM_E_PENDING: The process continues asynchronously; the DCM calls the API again in the next cycle of the DCM main function ([SWS_Dcm_01184]).
  • DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP: The application requests transmission of a response pending (NRC 0x78) ([SWS_Dcm_00543]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The conditions could not be saved.

Error handling

If the callout returns E_NOT_OK, the DCM initiates neither a reset nor a bootloader jump and does not switch DcmEcuReset to EXECUTE ([SWS_Dcm_01181]). Instead, the DCM aborts the action and sends a negative diagnostic response with NRC 0x22 (Conditions not correct) ([SWS_Dcm_00715]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification requirements of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.

The callout function Dcm_ProcessRequestDeleteFile ([SWS_Dcm_91079]) is called by the DCM module to initiate and execute a diagnostic process for the service RequestFileTransfer with mode 0x02 (DeleteFile).

Usage and Semantics

The function operates asynchronously and is non-reentrant (service ID 0x73, declared in Dcm_Externals.h). Processing progress is controlled via parameter OpStatus ([SWS_Dcm_91079]):

  • DCM_INITIAL: Initial call. The input parameters filePathAndNameLength and filePathAndName are valid and define the target path including the file name of the file to be deleted on the server.
  • DCM_PENDING, DCM_CANCEL, or DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK: Subsequent calls; all input parameters are set to 0x00.

Possible return values (Std_ReturnType) are:

  • E_OK: The deletion process completed successfully.
  • DCM_E_PENDING: Processing is not yet completed and requires further calls by the DCM.
  • DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP: The application requests transmission of an intermediate Response Pending message (NRC 0x78).
  • E_NOT_OK: The operation failed.

Error handling

The function Xxx_GetSeed ([SWS_Dcm_01151]) serves for the asynchronous provision of a seed value by the application and is provided via the header file Dcm_Externals.h. The call is made by the DCM submodule DSP upon receipt of the UDS service SecurityAccess (0x27) with the subfunction requestSeed, provided that the requested security level is not yet active ([SWS_Dcm_00862]).

Usage and Parameters

The function operates asynchronously and is defined as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant, service ID 0x44, [SWS_Dcm_01151]). It has the following interface parameters:

  • OpStatus: Passes the current execution status of the operation (Dcm_OpStatusType).
  • Seed: Output pointer for the seed provided by the application.
  • ErrorCode: Pointer for returning a negative response code (Dcm_NegativeResponseCodeType).

Return Values and Error Handling

Possible return values of Xxx_GetSeed are:

  • E_OK: The seed was provided successfully.
  • DCM_E_PENDING: The asynchronous operation is not yet completed; the DCM initiates further calls for completion.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request was not successful. In this case, the DCM sends a negative response with the NRC value passed in parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_01151], [SWS_Dcm_00659]).

The DCM calls Xxx_GetSeed depending on the configuration if DcmDspSecurityUsePort is set either to USE_ASYNCH_FNC ([SWS_Dcm_00862], referenced via DcmDspSecurityGetSeedFnc) or to USE_ASYNCH_CLIENT_SERVER ([SWS_Dcm_00324]). Request to application for asynchronous comparing key (DcmDspSecurityUsePort = USE_ ASYNCH_CLIENT_SERVER)

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 0e182c8c815f Provenance

Usage and Call Context

The function Xxx_CompareKey ([SWS_Dcm_91004]) is used for asynchronous key verification on the application side within the scope of the UDS service SecurityAccess (0x27) upon receipt of the subfunction sendKey. The DSP sub-module of the DCM calls this non-reentrant function if the required security level is not yet active and a seed was previously determined successfully ([SWS_Dcm_00324], [SWS_Dcm_00863]). The interface is available via Dcm_Externals.h for the configurations USE_ASYNCH_CLIENT_SERVER and USE_ASYNCH_FNC at parameter DcmDspSecurityUsePort.

Parameters and Return Values

The key to be compared is passed via Key, while OpStatus signals the progress of the asynchronous operation. The return value of type Std_ReturnType controls the further process ([SWS_Dcm_91004]):

  • E_OK: Key comparison was successful.
  • DCM_E_PENDING: Operation is not yet completed; further calls are required.
  • DCM_E_COMPARE_KEY_FAILED: The passed key does not match.
  • E_NOT_OK: The check was not successful; the NRC set via ErrorCode is sent to the client.

Error Handling and Interaction

The DCM module reacts in a differentiated manner to error states:

  • If Xxx_CompareKey returns the status E_NOT_OK, the DCM sends a negative response with the NRC from ErrorCode. The attempt counter (AttemptCounter) is not incremented and the security level remains unchanged ([SWS_Dcm_01150]).
  • If DCM_E_COMPARE_KEY_FAILED is returned and DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay is configured, the DCM increments the AttemptCounter ([SWS_Dcm_01397]). If the counter value is less than DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay, the DCM sends the negative response code NRC 0x35 (InvalidKey) ([SWS_Dcm_00660]). If it reaches or exceeds the limit value, the SecurityDelayTimer is started and NRC 0x36 (exceededNumberOfAttempts) is transmitted ([SWS_Dcm_01349]). In both cases, the internal security level remains unchanged.

Std_ReturnType Xxx_GetSecurityAttemptCounter (Dcm_OpStatusType OpStatus, uint8* AttemptCounter);

Read the attempt counter for a specific security level from the application

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 65ecf4f38f45 Provenance

The asynchronous, non-reentrant function Xxx_GetSecurityAttemptCounter ([SWS_Dcm_01152]) serves to read the failed attempt counter for a configured security level from the application. It is called during the initialization of the DCM for each entry DcmDspSecurityRow where the parameter DcmDspSecurityAttemptCounterEnabled is set to TRUE ([SWS_Dcm_01154]).

Parameters and Return Values

  • OpStatus: Passes the operation status (DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, or DCM_CANCEL) ([SWS_Dcm_01152]).
  • AttemptCounter: Pointer for returning the read counter value for the respective security level ([SWS_Dcm_01152]).
  • Return values: E_OK signals successful completion, E_NOT_OK an error, and DCM_E_PENDING that the operation has not yet finished and requires further calls ([SWS_Dcm_01152]).

Asynchronous Behavior and Error Handling

If the function returns DCM_E_PENDING, the DCM interrupts the call chain and resumes it in the next cycle of Dcm_MainFunction() ([SWS_Dcm_01351]). If the time period configured in DcmDspSecurityMaxAttemptCounterReadoutTime is reached before all calls are completed, the DCM aborts the still pending operation using OpStatus = DCM_CANCEL ([SWS_Dcm_01352]).

If Xxx_GetSecurityAttemptCounter returns the error E_NOT_OK, the failed attempt counter is set to the value stored in DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay of the respective security level ([SWS_Dcm_01156]).

Impact on SecurityAccess

As long as not all operations have reported a final status or have been aborted, the DCM answers each SecurityAccess request (0x27) for the subfunction requestSeed with the NRC conditionsNotCorrect (0x22) ([SWS_Dcm_01354]).

As soon as all counter values are finally available or the call chain has been aborted, the DCM checks whether at least one restored counter value is greater than or equal to DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay. If this is the case, the DCM starts the SecurityDelayTimer with the higher value from DcmDspSecurityDelayTimeOnBoot and DcmDspSecurityDelayTime of the corresponding security level ([SWS_Dcm_01355]).

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 9d9006e4fbcc Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The function Xxx_ReadData is declared via Dcm_Externals.h and called by the DCM module to query data values of a DID or PID from the application, provided that the parameter DcmDspDataUsePort is configured to USE_DATA_ASYNCH_CLIENT_SERVER [SWS_Dcm_91006]. Execution occurs asynchronously and is specified as non-reentrant [SWS_Dcm_91006].

The interface has the following parameters and return values [SWS_Dcm_91006]:

  • OpStatus (IN): Passes the current status of the running operation (Dcm_OpStatusType).
  • Data (OUT): Pointer to the buffer into which the requested user data is copied by the application.
  • Return value (Std_ReturnType): Returns E_OK if the query was completed successfully, or DCM_E_PENDING if processing is still ongoing and further calls are needed for completion.

Interaction and Service Context

The DCM incorporates the configured Xxx_ReadData functions into the processing of various diagnostic requests:

  • OBD Service $01: Upon reception of a Service $01 request for PIDs that are not availability PIDs, the DCM calls the configured Xxx_ReadData function for each datum of the PID and sends the obtained values as a response [SWS_Dcm_00408].
  • UDS Service 0x22 (ReadDataByIdentifier): For requests for OBDDataIdentifier or OBDInfoTypeDataIdentifier (except availability identifiers), the DCM queries the data values by calling the configured Xxx_ReadData functions for all associated data [SWS_Dcm_01380] [SWS_Dcm_01389].

The DCM module integrates configured Xxx_ReadData functions into the following diagnostic sequences:

The function Xxx_FreezeCurrentState (provided via Dcm_Externals.h) requests the application to freeze the current state of an I/O control (IOControl) [SWS_Dcm_01315].

Usage and Parameter Interface

The function has asynchronous semantics and is defined as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) [SWS_Dcm_01315]. The parameters are structured as follows:

  • OpStatus: Passes the current operation status (Dcm_OpStatusType) to control the asynchronous process.
  • controlMask or controlMask2: Optional input parameters in case of an externally configured control mask (DCM_CONTROLMASK_EXTERNAL). Depending on the mask size, type Dcm_ControlMask_{DID}Type (as controlMask) is passed for up to 4 bytes, and from 5 bytes a pointer uint8* (as controlMask2) is passed [SWS_Dcm_01315].
  • ErrorCode: Pointer to Dcm_NegativeResponseCodeType for returning a negative response code (NRC).

Return values (Std_ReturnType) according to [SWS_Dcm_01315]:

  • E_OK: Freezing the state was successfully completed.
  • DCM_E_PENDING: The request is still in progress; further follow-up calls by the DCM are required.
  • E_NOT_OK: The operation could not be executed successfully.

Error handling

If the application returns E_NOT_OK, it must output a specific NRC via parameter ErrorCode. In this case, the DCM sends a negative response with this code [SWS_Dcm_01315].

Concurrency and Limitations

Since the interface is non-reentrant, no concurrent call must occur for the same instance [SWS_Dcm_01315]. As long as DCM_E_PENDING is returned, the DCM controls subsequent calls via parameter OpStatus. The function Xxx_ShortTermAdjustment ([SWS_Dcm_00802]) requests the application to briefly adjust an I/O signal within the scope of the diagnostic service InputOutputControlByIdentifier. The interface is provided via the header Dcm_Externals.h.

Usage and Parameters

The call by the DCM takes place synchronously under the service ID 0x50. The passed parameters comprise:

  • ControlStateInfo (input): Pointer to the control status information from the ControlOptionRecord of the diagnostic request.
  • controlMask or controlMask2 (input, optional): Mask for signal selection. Depending on the configuration (USE_DATA_SYNCH_FNC and external mask mode), controlMask is passed for a mask size up to 4 bytes or controlMask2 starting from 5 bytes.
  • ErrorCode (output): Pointer to Dcm_NegativeResponseCodeType for reporting a negative response code (NRC).

Error Handling and Return Values

As Std_ReturnType, the function returns either E_OK on successful execution or E_NOT_OK in the event of an error. If the application returns E_NOT_OK, the DCM module sends a negative response with the NRC set in parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_00802]).

Concurrency and Interaction

The function is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Dcm_00802]). If an asynchronous interface is configured for data handling (such as USE_DATA_ASYNCH_FNC), the DCM uses the asynchronous variant of Xxx_ShortTermAdjustment ([SWS_Dcm_01316]) instead, which features additional parameters such as OpStatus and DataLength.

Upon receipt of a UDS request for RoutineControl (0x31) with the subfunction startRoutine, the DCM module calls the configured function Xxx_Start after successful verification ([SWS_Dcm_00400]). A call also takes place for RoutineControl requests with an OBDTestId that is not an availability ID ([SWS_Dcm_01392]).

The transfer comprises fixed input signals (dataIn_1 to dataIn_n) or variable input data (dataInVar) as well as the current status of the operation via OpStatus. In the case of variable data length, currentDataLength specifies the number of bytes of dataInVar or dataOutVar. The output data is provided via dataOut_1 to dataOut_n or dataOutVar. Possible return values are:

  • DCM_E_PENDING: The operation is not yet completed and requires subsequent calls.
  • DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP: The application requests transmission of a Response Pending (NRC 0x78).
  • E_NOT_OK: The operation was not successful. The DCM sends a negative response with the NRC specified in the output parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_01203]).

Error handling

If Xxx_Start returns a value other than E_OK in the context of an OBD routine request ([SWS_Dcm_01392]), the DCM responds with the negative response code NRC 0x22 ([SWS_Dcm_01394]).

function Xxx_StartProtocol [SWS_Dcm_01339] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Xxx_StartProtocol (Dcm_ProtocolType ProtocolType, uint16 TesterSourceAddress, uint16 ConnectionId);

This function allows the application to examine the environment conditions and enable/disable further processing of the protocol.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 3e89dede6bb0 Provenance

use

The synchronous callback function Xxx_StartProtocol ([SWS_Dcm_01339]), available via Dcm_Externals.h, allows the application to check environmental conditions and to enable or reject further protocol processing. Upon the first request of a diagnostic protocol, the DSL submodule calls all configured Xxx_StartProtocol functions ([SWS_Dcm_00036]). The protocol type to be started (ProtocolType), the tester source address (TesterSourceAddress), and the unique connection identifier (ConnectionId) are passed as input parameters ([SWS_Dcm_01339]).

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is designed to be synchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Dcm_01339]).

Error Handling and Return Values

Defined return values are E_OK (request successful), E_NOT_OK (request not successful), and E_PROTOCOL_NOT_ALLOWED (protocol not allowed) ([SWS_Dcm_01339]). Unless Xxx_StartProtocol returns E_OK, the DCM sends the negative response code NRC 0x22 ([SWS_Dcm_00674]).

Interaction during Protocol Start

Only after all configured Xxx_StartProtocol functions have returned E_OK, thus all components have permitted the start, does the DCM perform the following steps:

  • The standard timing parameters are loaded from the default session configuration ([SWS_Dcm_00144]).
  • The service table is set ([SWS_Dcm_00145]).
  • The security status is reset ([SWS_Dcm_00146]).
  • The session status is reset to the default session and the mode change is triggered via SchM_Switch_<bsnp>_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl(RTE_MODE_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl_DEFAULT_SESSION) ([SWS_Dcm_00147]).

This usage note is based on the specifications of AUTOSAR Release R20-11 for the DCM module.

Std_ReturnType Xxx_StopProtocol (Dcm_ProtocolType ProtocolType, uint16 TesterSourceAddress, uint16 ConnectionId);

This function informs the application of the protocol stop.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 1abce875f4c3 Provenance

The callback function Xxx_StopProtocol ([SWS_Dcm_01340]) informs the application about the termination of a diagnostic protocol. It is available via the header file Dcm_Externals.h, operates synchronously, and is defined as non-reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_01340]).

Usage and Call Context

The call is made by the submodule DSL (Diagnostic Session Layer) of the DCM. The following input parameters are passed to the function:

  • ProtocolType: Type of the protocol to be stopped ([SWS_Dcm_01340]).
  • TesterSourceAddress: Source address of the tester ([SWS_Dcm_01340]).
  • ConnectionId: Unique identifier of the affected connection ([SWS_Dcm_01340]).

Interaction and Preemption Rules

The DSL submodule calls all Xxx_StopProtocol functions registered via the configuration parameter DcmDslCallbackDCMRequestService when a protocol change or preemption occurs:

  • When an ongoing diagnostic request is preempted by a higher-priority request of another protocol ([SWS_Dcm_00459]).
  • When a request with equal or lower priority is allowed to preempt a higher-priority protocol because the latter is in the default session and no active request is being executed ([SWS_Dcm_00625]).

Error handling

As return value, E_OK signals successful processing and E_NOT_OK signals an error ([SWS_Dcm_01340]). If Xxx_StopProtocol does not return E_OK, the DCM responds with the negative response code NRC 0x22 ([SWS_Dcm_01190]).

The function Xxx_Indication ([SWS_Dcm_01341]) indicates the imminent execution of a diagnostic service to the application and enables it to reject the request. The call takes place synchronously and is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant); the declaration is provided via Dcm_Externals.h.

Call and Parameters

The function is called by the DSD submodule of the DCM provided that corresponding notification containers are configured ([SWS_Dcm_00218], [SWS_Dcm_00516]). The service identifier SID, the diagnostic data RequestData without SID with the number of valid bytes DataSize, the addressing type ReqType (physical or functional), the connection identifier ConnectionId, the protocol type ProtocolType, and the tester address TesterSourceAddress, among others, are passed ([SWS_Dcm_01341]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The application controls the further behavior of the DCM via the return value:

  • E_OK: The service request has been accepted successfully ([SWS_Dcm_01341]).
  • E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED: If at least one called indication function returns this value, the DSD submodule sends no response whatsoever to the tester ([SWS_Dcm_00462], [SWS_Dcm_00517]).
  • E_NOT_OK: Unless any call returns E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED, the DSD submodule initiates a negative response (NRC) with the value set via the output parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_00463], [SWS_Dcm_00518], [SWS_Dcm_01341]).

If multiple indication functions return E_NOT_OK (and none returns E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED), the DSD submodule uses the ErrorCode of the function that was first in time to return E_NOT_OK for the negative response ([SWS_Dcm_01321], [SWS_Dcm_01322]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.

The synchronous function Xxx_Confirmation ([SWS_Dcm_01342]) confirms the successful transmission or a transmission error of a diagnostic service to the application. It is available via the header file Dcm_Externals.h, has the service ID 0x66, and is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).

Usage and Parameters

The function passes context information regarding the completed diagnostic transmission to the application ([SWS_Dcm_01342]):

  • SID: Value of the service identifier ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • ReqType: Addressing type of the request (0 for physical requests, 1 for functional requests) ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • ConnectionId: Unique identifier of the connection ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • ConfirmationStatus: Confirmation status regarding a successful transmission or a transmission error ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • ProtocolType: Type of the DCM protocol ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • TesterSourceAddress: Source address of the tester ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).

Xxx_Confirmation returns the type Std_ReturnType with E_OK (request successful) or E_NOT_OK (request unsuccessful) as the return value ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).

Call Context and Interaction

The DSD submodule calls the operation Xxx_Confirmation() on all ports that use the interface ServiceRequestNotification ([SWS_Dcm_00741]). This affects ports of the configuration parameters DcmDsdServiceRequestManufacturerNotification and DcmDsdServiceRequestSupplierNotification ([SWS_Dcm_00741]).

Regarding the sequence, it is specified that the call to Xxx_Confirmation() must occur directly after the call to DspInternal_DcmConfirmation() ([SWS_Dcm_00742]). In the special case according to [SWS_Dcm_01172], however, the DSD submodule exclusively calls Xxx_Confirmation() and suppresses the call to DspInternal_DcmConfirmation() ([SWS_Dcm_01172]).

function Xxx_ProcessRequestDownload [SWS_Dcm_00754] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Xxx_ProcessRequestDownload (Dcm_OpStatusType OpStatus, uint8 DataFormatIdentifier, uint8 MemoryIdentifier, uint32 MemoryAddress, uint32 MemorySize, uint32* BlockLength, Dcm_NegativeResponseCodeType* ErrorCode);

Callout function. DCM shall call this callout function to start a download process. This service is needed for the implementation of UDS service RequestDownload.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 44c0feb2b90e Provenance

Usage and Call Context

The callout function Xxx_ProcessRequestDownload ([SWS_Dcm_00754]) is called by module Dcm to start the download process for the implementation of the UDS service RequestDownload. The declaration is available via Dcm_Externals.h. The function operates asynchronously and is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Dcm_00754]).

When called, the parameter OpStatus controls the processing state with the values DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, or DCM_CANCEL ([SWS_Dcm_00754]). Compression methods (bits 7–4) and encryption methods (bits 3–0) are passed via DataFormatIdentifier. Additional input parameters define the memory block (MemoryIdentifier, 0 if not used), the starting address in server memory (MemoryAddress), and the uncompressed memory size in bytes (MemorySize) ([SWS_Dcm_00754]).

Prior to execution, the DCM writes the maximum possible buffer size into the in/out parameter BlockLength ([SWS_Dcm_01417]). This parameter defines the maximum number of bytes for individual subsequent Dcm_WriteMemory calls ([SWS_Dcm_00754]).

Return Values and Interaction

  • E_OK: The download start was successful ([SWS_Dcm_00754]). If the returned BlockLength value is less than or equal to the supported buffer length of the current protocol connection, the DCM returns this value in parameter maxNumberOfBlockLength of the positive response ([SWS_Dcm_01419]).
  • DCM_E_PENDING: The request is not yet completed and requires follow-up calls ([SWS_Dcm_00754]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed ([SWS_Dcm_00754]). The DCM subsequently sends a negative UDS response (NRC) with the value provided by the function via the output parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_00754], [SWS_Dcm_00757]).

Error handling

If the function returns a value for BlockLength that exceeds the supported buffer length of the current protocol connection, the DCM reports the DET error DCM_E_INTERFACE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW ([SWS_Dcm_01418]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification.

Usage and Flow

The callout function Xxx_ProcessRequestTransferExit is called by the DCM module to terminate an ongoing download or upload process within the scope of the UDS service RequestTransferExit ([SWS_Dcm_00755]). The declaration is provided via the header file Dcm_Externals.h; the service has the service ID 0x32 ([SWS_Dcm_00755]).

Execution is asynchronous and is non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Dcm_00755]). The DCM module controls the termination progress via the passed parameter OpStatus of type Dcm_OpStatusType:

  • DCM_INITIAL: Initiates the completion of the data transfer ([SWS_Dcm_00755]).
  • DCM_PENDING: Signals repeated calls to continue an operation that is not yet completed ([SWS_Dcm_00755]).
  • DCM_CANCEL: Cancels the ongoing termination of the transfer ([SWS_Dcm_00755]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The function returns its current processing status via the return value Std_ReturnType ([SWS_Dcm_00755]):

  • E_OK: The transfer was terminated successfully ([SWS_Dcm_00755]).
  • DCM_E_PENDING: The transmission or termination is not yet completed ([SWS_Dcm_00755]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The transfer was not successful or the response buffer is too small ([SWS_Dcm_00755]).

If the operation returns E_NOT_OK, an appropriate error code (Dcm_NegativeResponseCodeType) must be set via the output parameter ErrorCode. The DCM module then sends a negative response (Negative Response) with the passed NRC value ([SWS_Dcm_00759]).

use

The callout function Xxx_ProcessRequestUpload ([SWS_Dcm_00756]) is called by the DCM module to start the upload process within the scope of the UDS service RequestUpload. The declaration is provided via Dcm_Externals.h ([SWS_Dcm_00756]).

The call takes place with the following parameters ([SWS_Dcm_00756]):

  • OpStatus: Operation status of the service (possible values: DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, DCM_CANCEL, or DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK).
  • DataFormatIdentifier: Specifies the compression method (bits 7–4; 0x0: uncompressed) and the encryption method (bits 3–0; 0x0: unencrypted).
  • MemoryIdentifier: Identifier of the memory block (set to 0 if not used).
  • MemoryAddress and MemorySize: Starting address of the server memory as well as uncompressed memory size in bytes.
  • BlockLength: Inout parameter for the maximum block size. Before the call, the DCM writes the maximum possible buffer size into this parameter ([SWS_Dcm_01420]); the function returns the maximum byte count for an individual Dcm_ReadMemory process in it ([SWS_Dcm_00756]).
  • ErrorCode: Output parameter for the negative response code (NRC).

Valid return values are E_OK upon successful execution, DCM_E_PENDING while asynchronous processing is still ongoing, and E_NOT_OK in the event of an error ([SWS_Dcm_00756]).

Concurrency and Interaction

The function is defined as asynchronous and non-reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_00756]). If the buffer value returned by the function via BlockLength is less than or equal to the supported buffer length of the current protocol connection, the DCM applies this value to parameter maxNumberOfBlockLength of the positive UDS response ([SWS_Dcm_01422]).

Error handling

If the call returns E_NOT_OK, the DCM module sends a negative UDS response with the NRC provided in parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_00756], [SWS_Dcm_00758]). If the function requests a buffer length in BlockLength that is greater than the supported buffer size of the current connection, the DCM reports the DET error DCM_E_INTERFACE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW ([SWS_Dcm_01421]).

Dcm_ReturnReadMemoryType Xxx_ProcessTransferDataRead (Dcm_OpStatusType OpStatus, uint8 MemoryIdentifier, uint32 MemoryAddress, uint32 MemorySize, Dcm_RequestDataArrayType MemoryData, Dcm_NegativeResponseCodeType* ErrorCode);

The ProcessTransferDataRead callout is used to request memory data identified by the parameter memoryAddress and memorySize from the UDS request message. This service is needed for the implementation of UDS services: • ReadMemoryByAddress • RequestUpload • ReadDataByIdentifier (in case of Dynamical DID defined by memory address) • TransferData

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: b3ef7d01745f Provenance

The callout function Xxx_ProcessTransferDataRead ([SWS_Dcm_91070]) serves to retrieve memory data based on the parameters MemoryAddress and MemorySize from a UDS request message. It is required for the implementation of the UDS services ReadMemoryByAddress, RequestUpload, ReadDataByIdentifier (for DIDs dynamically defined via memory address), as well as TransferData, and is provided via the header file Dcm_Externals.h.

Usage and Semantics

The function operates asynchronously and is defined as non-reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_91070]). The call context is controlled via the progress status OpStatus:

  • DCM_INITIAL: First call to initiate the read operation.
  • DCM_PENDING: Follow-up processing of an uncompleted read operation.
  • DCM_CANCEL: Request to abort the ongoing read operation.
  • DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK: Confirmation after transmission of a forced waiting response (Response Pending).

The data to be read is written directly into the diagnostic buffer of the DCM via the output parameter MemoryData. MemoryIdentifier identifies the memory block (if not used, the value must be set to 0), while MemoryAddress defines the starting address and MemorySize the number of bytes to be read ([SWS_Dcm_91070]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The return type Dcm_ReturnReadMemoryType signals the operation result:

  • DCM_READ_OK: The read operation was terminated successfully.
  • DCM_READ_PENDING: The read operation is ongoing and requires further cycles.
  • DCM_READ_FORCE_RCRRP: The process is still pending; transmission of a Response Pending (RCR-RP) starts immediately.
  • DCM_READ_FAILED: The read operation failed. In this case, the output parameter ErrorCode must be set, whereupon the DCM module transmits a negative response with this NRC code ([SWS_Dcm_91070]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR R20-11 specification status.

The input parameter MemoryData directly references the diagnostic buffer of the DCM.   • DCM_WRITE_FAILED: The write operation was unsuccessful. In this case, the DCM module transmits a negative response with the NRC value passed in output parameter ErrorCode.

type Dcm_StatusType [SWS_Dcm_00976] 📄 PDF

Base item type to transport status information.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: b598b559c349 Provenance

According to [SWS_Dcm_00976], the data type Dcm_StatusType serves as a base type for transporting status information within the Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM). It is derived from the base type uint8 and is made available via the header file Dcm.h.

Usage and Status Values

Dcm_StatusType is used as a return type for specific DCM functions to indicate the execution status or the acceptance of a service request. The following values are defined in [SWS_Dcm_00976]:

  • DCM_E_OK (0x00): Signals a successful operation [SWS_Dcm_00976].
  • DCM_E_ROE_NOT_ACCEPTED (0x06): Indicates that a ResponseOnOneEvent request was not accepted by the DCM (for example because a preceding ResponseOnOneEvent action is not yet completed). This status value is used at the interface Dcm_ResponseOnOneEvent() [SWS_Dcm_00976].
  • DCM_E_PERIODICID_NOT_ACCEPTED (0x07): Indicates that a periodic transmission request was rejected by the DCM (for example because a preceding periodic transmission has not yet finished). This return value is returned at the interface Dcm_ResponseOnOneDataByPeriodicId() [SWS_Dcm_00976].

Error Handling and Concurrency

The error values DCM_E_ROE_NOT_ACCEPTED and DCM_E_PERIODICID_NOT_ACCEPTED refer to timing dependencies and sequencing conditions: The DCM rejects new requests as long as a previous operation of the same type is still in progress. Calling components must evaluate these return values to detect whether a request was rejected [SWS_Dcm_00976].

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification for Dcm_StatusType.

type Dcm_CommunicationModeType [SWS_Dcm_00981] 📄 PDF

 Manager

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 005a1c1137c2 Provenance

The data type Dcm_CommunicationModeType ([SWS_Dcm_00981]) is based on uint8 and represents the communication control state regarding transmission (Tx) and reception (Rx). The enumeration values in the range from 0x00 to 0x0B cover normal messages (NORM), network management (NM), and their combination (NORM_NM).

Usage and Interaction

The type is primarily used to pass the requested communication state for the UDS service CommunicationControl (0x28) to the BSW Manager (BswM). After successful confirmation of the transmitted diagnostic response (Sent Confirmation), the DCM calls the function BswM_Dcm_CommunicationMode_CurrentState with the affected network handle (NetworkHandleType) and the determined mode (Dcm_CommunicationModeType):

  • All channels: When the subnet parameter 0x00 is specified, switching takes place for each network handle configured in DcmDspComControlAllChannel ([SWS_Dcm_00512]).
  • Current receiving network: With subnet 0x0F, the communication mode is set for the network of the currently received request ([SWS_Dcm_00785]).
  • Specific subnets: For subnet parameters in the range from 0x01 to 0x0E, the mode is applied to the associated network channel ([SWS_Dcm_00786]).
  • Enhanced addressing: For subfunctions such as enableRxAndDisableTxWithEnhancedAddressInformation ([SWS_Dcm_01077]) or enableRxAndTxWithEnhancedAddressInformation ([SWS_Dcm_01079]), the channel referenced via DcmDspComControlSubNodeComMChannelRef is updated.

Error handling

If a subnet number between 0x01 and 0x0E is requested that is not supported, processing is aborted and the DCM responds with the negative response code (NRC) 0x31 ([SWS_Dcm_00786]); a call for mode change to the BswM is omitted in this case.

This usage note is based exclusively on the specifications of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.
