AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 84a9222183b8 Provenance

The type Dcm_EcuStartModeType is an enumeration type derived from uint8 that signals to the Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM) whether the ECU starts regularly or whether there is a start resulting from a jump from the bootloader where a final diagnostic response is to be sent [SWS_Dcm_00987].

Value Range and Semantics

  • DCM_COLD_START (0x00): The ECU starts in a regular manner (cold start) [SWS_Dcm_00987].
  • DCM_WARM_START (0x01): The ECU starts from a preceding bootloader jump (warm start) [SWS_Dcm_00987].

The data type is provided via the header Dcm.h [SWS_Dcm_00987].

Interaction and Usage

Dcm_EcuStartModeType serves as the return value of the synchronous callout function Dcm_GetProgConditions [SWS_Dcm_00544]. This function is called during the initialization of the DCM to determine, based on the returned start mode, whether a diagnostic response (e.g. to service $50 or $51) must be transmitted [SWS_Dcm_00544].

Additional context information regarding the conditions of the bootloader jump is passed via the output parameter ProgConditions of type Dcm_ProgConditionsType* [SWS_Dcm_00544]. The callout interface is defined as non-reentrant and is declared via Dcm_Externals.h [SWS_Dcm_00544].

This usage note was created automatically based on the specification for AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

The structure Dcm_ProgConditionsType ([SWS_Dcm_00988]) is used to exchange context and state data during the transition between application and bootloader, for example as a result of reprogramming or an ECU reset (ECUReset).

Usage and Interfaces

The structure is used in two central interfaces:

  • Before the jump: The asynchronous, non-reentrant function Dcm_SetProgConditions() ([SWS_Dcm_00543]) accepts a pointer const Dcm_ProgConditionsType* ProgConditions to save the relevant conditions before switching to the bootloader.
  • After the restart: The synchronous callout Dcm_GetProgConditions() ([SWS_Dcm_00544]) populates the output parameter ProgConditions during initialization of the DCM to determine the start mode and evaluate whether a pending diagnostic response must be sent.

Structure Fields and Interaction

The structure fields control the further behavior of diagnostic communication:

  • ConnectionId and TesterAddress: Identify the connection and the source address of the tester ([SWS_Dcm_00988]).
  • Sid and SubFncId: Identify the service and subfunction identifier of the received request. If ComM reports full communication, the DCM sends the response for the stored Sid ([SWS_Dcm_00767]).
  • ResponseRequired: Specifies whether the flashloader or application must send a confirmation (e.g. Response $50 or $51) after the switch ([SWS_Dcm_00988], [SWS_Dcm_00544]).
  • ReprogramingRequest: Signals the request for reprogramming the ECU ([SWS_Dcm_00988]).
  • ApplUpdated: Indicates whether the application was updated via flash download. If this is the case after a jump from the bootloader (ApplUpdated == True), the DCM notifies the BswM by means of BswM_Dcm_ApplicationUpdated() ([SWS_Dcm_00768]).

The data type Dcm_MsgType is the base type for diagnostic messages in the DCM module and is available via the header Dcm.h ([SWS_Dcm_00990]). It is defined as a pointer to message elements (Dcm_MsgItemType*) and is used to address raw data buffers for diagnostic requests as well as for positive or negative response messages ([SWS_Dcm_00990]).

Interaction and Buffer Semantics

A central use of Dcm_MsgType is within the context structure Dcm_MsgContextType ([SWS_Dcm_00994]). There it types the data pointers:

  • reqData: Points to the payload of the incoming diagnostic request ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).
  • resData: Serves as a buffer pointer for the positive response data to be generated ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).

For both fields, the data referenced via Dcm_MsgType starts immediately after the Service Identifier (SID); the SID itself is not part of these buffer segments ([SWS_Dcm_00994]). The associated data length is managed separately via parameters of type Dcm_MsgLenType (such as reqDataLen and resDataLen) ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).

restrictions

When writing response data via resData, the maximum buffer size specified by resMaxDataLen must strictly be observed to prevent buffer overflows ([SWS_Dcm_00994]). The provided pointer presumably typically references directly the linear communication buffer allocated by the DCM.

This note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR Classic R20-11 specification.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 85d290bdb37c Provenance

The type Dcm_MsgLenType describes the length of a diagnostic message (request, positive, or negative response) within the module DCM ([SWS_Dcm_00991]). It is derived from the base type uint32 and is provided via the header Dcm.h ([SWS_Dcm_00991]).

The maximum permissible or processable message length depends on the respective underlying transport protocol or the transmission media used ([SWS_Dcm_00991]).

In interaction with diagnostic requests and responses, Dcm_MsgLenType is used as the type for several length fields of the structure Dcm_MsgContextType ([SWS_Dcm_00994]):

  • reqDataLen: Specifies the length of the request data (reqData), calculated without the service identifier ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).
  • resDataLen: Indicates the length of the positive response data (resData), likewise excluding the service identifier ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).
  • resMaxDataLen: Defines the maximum response length, which is strictly limited by the dimensioning of the assigned buffer ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).

Interpretation: Although the data type uint32 theoretically opens up very large value ranges, the actual length of a diagnostic message in practice is likely always limited by the transport medium and the buffer size stored in resMaxDataLen ([SWS_Dcm_00991], [SWS_Dcm_00994]).

type Dcm_MsgAddInfoType [SWS_Dcm_00992] 📄 PDF

Additional information on message request. Datastructure: Bitfield

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: b2b128343dd3 Provenance

According to [SWS_Dcm_00992], the data type Dcm_MsgAddInfoType is defined as a bit field structure and is available via the header file Dcm.h. The structure serves to transmit additional control and status information for a diagnostic request.

Structure and Bit Allocation

According to [SWS_Dcm_00992], the type contains the following bit elements:

  • reqType (position LSB+0): Indicates the addressing type of the request. The value 0 indicates a physical request, the value 1 a functional request.
  • suppressPosResponse (position LSB+1): Controls the suppression of a positive response. The value 0 means that the positive response is sent (do not suppress), while 1 specifies that no positive response may be sent (no positive response will be sent).

Interaction

According to [SWS_Dcm_00994], Dcm_MsgAddInfoType is embedded as element msgAddInfo in the higher-level message structure Dcm_MsgContextType. This gives processing functions in the DCM access to the request type as well as the information whether sending the positive response must be suppressed.

type Dcm_MsgContextType [SWS_Dcm_00994] 📄 PDF

This data structure contains all information which is necessary to process a diagnostic message from request to response and response confirmation.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 3c4b9dcad543 Provenance

Usage and Call Context

The data structure Dcm_MsgContextType bundles all relevant information to process a diagnostic message from request to response and down to confirmation ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).\n It is passed to diagnostic service and sub-service functions such as <Module>_<DiagnosticService> as an input/output parameter (pMsgContext); these operations are asynchronous and reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_00763], [SWS_Dcm_00764]).\n The data pointers reqData and resData always point directly behind the service identifier (SID), so that both reqDataLen and resDataLen do not include the SID length ([SWS_Dcm_00994], [SWS_Dcm_00763]).

Interaction and Lifecycle

The DSD submodule inserts the response SID at the first byte position of the buffer and transmits the response data stream ([SWS_Dcm_00223], [SWS_Dcm_00224]).\n Additional information is transmitted via msgAddInfo: If the suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit is set there, the DSD submodule activates positive response suppression ([SWS_Dcm_00202], [SWS_Dcm_00231]).\n Via the element idContext, the application can correlate the confirmation to the original request, since the context becomes invalid upon confirmation and all message data is lost ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).

Error Handling and Buffer Limitation

The maximum response length is specified protocol-specifically via resMaxDataLen ([SWS_Dcm_00994]).\n If DcmPagedBufferEnabled == FALSE is configured and the generated response exceeds this maximum length, the DCM sends a negative response with NRC 0x14 (DCM_E_RESPONSETOOLONG) ([SWS_Dcm_01059]).

type Dcm_ExtendedOpStatusType [SWS_Dcm_91015] 📄 PDF



AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 2acdef8d7ee3 Provenance

Usage of Dcm_ExtendedOpStatusType

The type Dcm_ExtendedOpStatusType ([SWS_Dcm_91015]) is derived from uint8 and is provided via Dcm.h. It serves as input parameter OpStatus for control and status feedback during the asynchronous execution of diagnostic services via <Module>_<DiagnosticService> ([SWS_Dcm_00763]) and sub-services via <Module>_<DiagnosticService>_<SubService> ([SWS_Dcm_00764]).

The defined values control the phases of operation processing:

  • DCM_INITIAL (0x00): Indicates the initial call of the operation.
  • DCM_PENDING (0x01): Indicates that a pending feedback occurred during the previous call of the operation.
  • DCM_CANCEL (0x02): Signals the request of the DCM module to cancel the still pending operation.
  • DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK (0x03): Confirms the transmission of a pending response (Response Pending).
  • DCM_POS_RESPONSE_SENT (0x04) and DCM_POS_RESPONSE_FAILED (0x05): Indicate that a positive response was transmitted successfully and unsuccessfully, respectively.
  • DCM_NEG_RESPONSE_SENT (0x06) and DCM_NEG_RESPONSE_FAILED (0x07): Indicate that a negative response was transmitted successfully and unsuccessfully, respectively.

Concurrency and Error Handling: The calling service operations are defined as asynchronous and reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_00763], [SWS_Dcm_00764]). If the service operation yields the return value E_NOT_OK, the DCM module sends a negative response with the negative response code (NRC) provided via the output parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_00763], [SWS_Dcm_00764]).

This usage note is based on the specification elements of the AUTOSAR DCM module in release R20-11.

type Dcm_OpStatusType [SWS_Dcm_00984] 📄 PDF



AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d3c7fe348695 Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The type Dcm_OpStatusType ([SWS_Dcm_00984]) controls the execution status of asynchronous diagnostic operations in the DCM and is provided via Rte_Dcm_Type.h ([SWS_Dcm_00984]). The type derived from uint8 defines the following states ([SWS_Dcm_00984]):

  • DCM_INITIAL (0x00): Indicates the initial first call of the operation ([SWS_Dcm_00984]). The DCM always calls an operation with this status on the first call ([SWS_Dcm_00527]).
  • DCM_PENDING (0x01): Indicates that the previous call was not yet completed ([SWS_Dcm_00984]). If an operation returns the return value DCM_E_PENDING, the DCM calls it in every cycle of Dcm_MainFunction with OpStatus = DCM_PENDING as long as DCM_E_PENDING is returned ([SWS_Dcm_00530]).
  • DCM_CANCEL (0x02): Signals the DCM request to cancel the ongoing asynchronous operation ([SWS_Dcm_00984]).
  • DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK (0x03): Confirms the transmission of a pending response (Response Pending) ([SWS_Dcm_00984]). If an operation returns DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP, the DCM initiates the sending of RCR-RP (NRC 0x78) and suspends further calls to the operation until RCR-RP has been sent ([SWS_Dcm_00528]).

Concurrency and Call Context

DCM interfaces that accept Dcm_OpStatusType as a parameter—such as memory operations like Dcm_ReadMemory ([SWS_Dcm_00539]) and Dcm_WriteMemory ([SWS_Dcm_00540]), process controls like Dcm_SetProgConditions ([SWS_Dcm_00543]), and transfer routines like Xxx_ProcessRequestDownload ([SWS_Dcm_00754]) and Xxx_ProcessRequestUpload ([SWS_Dcm_00756])—are defined as asynchronous and non-reentrant.

type Dcm_ConfirmationStatusType [SWS_Dcm_00983] 📄 PDF



AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 3dc24ab9ff4c Provenance

use

The type Dcm_ConfirmationStatusType is derived from uint8 and is available via Rte_Dcm_Type.h [SWS_Dcm_00983]. It represents the confirmation status of a diagnostic transmission and defines four discrete values [SWS_Dcm_00983]:

  • DCM_RES_POS_OK (0x00): Positive response successfully transmitted
  • DCM_RES_POS_NOT_OK (0x01): Positive response transmitted with error
  • DCM_RES_NEG_OK (0x02): Negative response successfully transmitted
  • DCM_RES_NEG_NOT_OK (0x03): Negative response transmitted with error

Interaction and Interfaces

The status is used as input parameter ConfirmationStatus in various confirmation contexts of the DCM:

  • In the operation Confirmation of the service interface ServiceRequestNotification to notify about the termination of a service request [SWS_Dcm_00694].
  • In the callback function Xxx_Confirmation to acknowledge a successful transmission or a transmission error of a diagnostic service [SWS_Dcm_01342].
  • In the confirmation functions for routines according to Dcm_Externals.h: Xxx_StartConfirmation for StartRoutine requests [SWS_Dcm_91016], Xxx_StopConfirmation for StopRoutine requests [SWS_Dcm_91017], and Xxx_RequestResultsConfirmation for routine result queries [SWS_Dcm_91018].

Concurrency and Error Handling

The interfaces Xxx_Confirmation [SWS_Dcm_01342], Xxx_StartConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_91016], Xxx_StopConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_91017] and Xxx_RequestResultsConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_91018] are synchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). Transmission errors are notified to the caller via the error values DCM_RES_POS_NOT_OK or DCM_RES_NEG_NOT_OK [SWS_Dcm_00983]. The confirmation functions return Std_ReturnType (E_OK on successful processing, E_NOT_OK on errors) as return value [SWS_Dcm_01342], [SWS_Dcm_91016], [SWS_Dcm_91017], [SWS_Dcm_91018].

The data type Dcm_AuthenticationRoleType ([SWS_Dcm_91068]) defines a byte array (base element uint8) for mapping authentication roles in the DCM module. The length of this array is determined via configuration parameter DcmDspAuthenticationRoleSize. The type is provided via the header Rte_Dcm_Type.h.

Usage and Interaction

The type represents role information and is passed primarily when configuring default roles for unauthenticated connections:

  • In the C API, Dcm_AuthenticationRoleType serves as input parameter deauthenticatedRole of the service function Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole ([SWS_Dcm_91069]). Here, the connection referenced via connectionId is assigned a new role for the \"deauthenticated\" state.
  • At the level of the AUTOSAR software components, the same type is used in the service interface Authentication as an IN parameter of the operation SetDeauthenticatedRole ([SWS_Dcm_91072]).
  • The role set with this type remains active for the respective connection until the connection transitions to the authenticated state or an ECU reset occurs ([SWS_Dcm_91069], [SWS_Dcm_91072]).

Concurrency and return values

The processing of the type via Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole ([SWS_Dcm_91069]) is implemented synchronously and reentrantly. As the return value, exclusively E_OK is specified both for the C API and for the service operation SetDeauthenticatedRole ([SWS_Dcm_91072]).

Usage and Interaction

The DCM acts as a mode manager for diagnostic modes and provides DcmSecurityAccess as a provided mode group (provided-ModeGroup) in the context of the UDS service 0x27 (SecurityAccess) ([SWS_Dcm_00775], [SWS_Dcm_01327]):

  • Mode configuration: In addition to the base state DCM_SEC_LEV_LOCKED, further security levels such as DCM_SEC_LEV_1 to DCM_SEC_LEV_63 are added via configuration rows (DcmDspSecurityRow) ([SWS_Dcm_91031], [SWS_Dcm_01327]).
  • Status update: Upon each change of the security level, the DCM updates the mode group with the new level ([SWS_Dcm_01329]).
  • SW-C connection: Software components (SW-Cs) that must be informed about the current security status connect the service interface Dcm_SecurityAccessModeSwitchInterface with the mode group securityAccess ([SWS_Dcm_91032]).

Restrictions and Error Handling

Since this is a mode declaration group, there are no direct error codes or DET/DEM messages at the data type level. Consuming SW-Cs are typically expected to be notified of state changes via corresponding mode switch mechanisms of the RTE.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification requirements.

Callbacks

Dcm_CopyRxData function

This function is called to provide the received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer. Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data. The size of the remaining buffer is written to the position indicated by bufferSizePtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_CopyRxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);
Dcm_CopyTxData function

This function is called to acquire the transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data unless retry->TpDataState is TP_ DATARETRY. In this case the function restarts to copy the data beginning at the offset from the current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to the position indicated by availableDataPtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_CopyTxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, const RetryInfoType* retry, PduLengthType* availableDataPtr);
Dcm_StartOfReception function

This function is called at the start of receiving an N-SDU. The N-SDU might be fragmented into multiple N-PDUs (FF with one or more following CFs) or might consist of a single N-PDU (SF). The service shall provide the currently available maximum buffer size when invoked with TpSdu Length equal to 0. This function might be called in interrupt context.

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_StartOfReception (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType TpSduLength, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);
Dcm_TpRxIndication function

Called after an I-PDU has been received via the TP API, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not. This function might be called in interrupt context.

void Dcm_TpRxIndication (PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);
Dcm_TpTxConfirmation function

This function is called after the I-PDU has been transmitted on its network, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not. This function might be called in interrupt context.

void Dcm_TpTxConfirmation (PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);
Dcm_TxConfirmation function

The lower layer communication interface module confirms the transmission of a PDU, or the failure to transmit a PDU. This function might be called in interrupt context.

void Dcm_TxConfirmation (PduIdType TxPduId, Std_ReturnType result);
